Hello João @jvalverde,

commit 7160b4b1771dd308ac3a1423ca03215741772c55 on macOS 10.15.7 build system fails with:

```
/Users/jyoung/projects/wireshark/wsutil/crash_info.c:134:6: error: implicit declaration of function 'ws_strdup_vprintf' is invalid in C99 [-Werror,-Wimplicit-function-declaration]
        m = ws_strdup_vprintf(fmt, ap);
            ^
/Users/jyoung/projects/wireshark/wsutil/crash_info.c:134:6: note: did you mean 'g_strdup_vprintf'?
/usr/local/include/glib-2.0/glib/gstrfuncs.h:222:22: note: 'g_strdup_vprintf' declared here
gchar*                g_strdup_vprintf (const gchar *format,
                      ^
/Users/jyoung/projects/wireshark/wsutil/crash_info.c:134:6: error: this function declaration is not a prototype [-Werror,-Wstrict-prototypes]
        m = ws_strdup_vprintf(fmt, ap);
            ^
/Users/jyoung/projects/wireshark/wsutil/crash_info.c:134:4: error: incompatible integer to pointer conversion assigning to 'char *' from 'int' [-Werror,-Wint-conversion]
        m = ws_strdup_vprintf(fmt, ap);
          ^ ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
/Users/jyoung/projects/wireshark/wsutil/crash_info.c:139:14: error: implicit declaration of function 'ws_strdup_printf' is invalid in C99 [-Werror,-Wimplicit-function-declaration]
                new_info = ws_strdup_printf("%s\n%s", old_info, m);
                           ^
/Users/jyoung/projects/wireshark/wsutil/crash_info.c:139:14: note: did you mean 'ws_strdup_vprintf'?
/Users/jyoung/projects/wireshark/wsutil/crash_info.c:134:6: note: 'ws_strdup_vprintf' declared here
        m = ws_strdup_vprintf(fmt, ap);
            ^
/Users/jyoung/projects/wireshark/wsutil/crash_info.c:139:14: error: this function declaration is not a prototype [-Werror,-Wstrict-prototypes]
                new_info = ws_strdup_printf("%s\n%s", old_info, m);
                           ^
/Users/jyoung/projects/wireshark/wsutil/crash_info.c:139:12: error: incompatible integer to pointer conversion assigning to 'char *' from 'int' [-Werror,-Wint-conversion]
                new_info = ws_strdup_printf("%s\n%s", old_info, m);
                         ^ ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
6 errors generated.
```
Thanks, missing header hidden behind conditional compilation. I will push a fix as soon as I can (later today).

Presumably by "C library I/O" you mean "C library formatted output routines"; I'm not seeing a change to use `FILE *`s instead of something else and *am* seeing changes to the way formatting is done in memory (`snprintf()` isn't an "I/O" routine in terms of reading from or writing to a file/socket/pipe/device).

The program, in case it isn't clear, it to replace Gnulib with the C library and consistently use native I/O functions. I didn't replace anything using FILE * because there was nothing left to replace.
Something like that. I am including formatted strings under the umbrella of I/O. Specifically "O".

> commit 7160b4b1771dd308ac3a1423ca03215741772c55 on macOS 10.15.7 build system fails with:

Fixed in !5503.

commits_data.title: wmem: Add ws_strdup_printf() convenience macros
commits_data.message:
wmem: Add ws_strdup_printf() convenience macros

The convention (for wmem) is that functions with ws_ use
malloc'ed memory. This is just a convenience to avoid having
to pass a NULL allocator.
